abstract: Endogenous retroviruses (ERVs) are genomic remnants of ancient retroviral infections that provide a record of host-virus evolution and contribute to the structure, regulation, and function of host genomes. ERV Navigator addresses a longstanding challenge in ERV research: the absence of a unified, evolutionarily informed framework that reconciles existing annotation systems, nomenclatures, and classification schemes. Existing resources provide complementary views of human ERVs (HERVs), reflecting different discovery strategies, biological objectives, and historical conventions, making comparisons across studies and integration of evolutionary and functional data difficult. ERV Navigator integrates major HERV annotation resources within a single, non-redundant reference framework centered on genomic loci and their evolutionary relationships. The database organizes information hierarchically, linking retroviral taxonomy, lineage-level reference sequences, and genomic insertions through stable, phylogenetically informed identifiers. Historical nomenclatures and annotations are preserved through explicit cross-references, enabling seamless navigation between legacy resources and the unified framework. The web interface supports taxonomic browsing, phylogenetic visualization, lineage and locus pages, genome browser integration, sequence alignments, and search tools. By combining evolutionary classification with genomic, structural, and functional annotations, ERV Navigator enables reproducible comparison of HERV loci while providing a flexible platform for comparative, functional, and disease-associated data. ERV Navigator is freely available at https://ervnavigator.fredhutch.org/.
